title: Finite bit construction: one extra XOR reaches the J3 positive-envelope floor (no new kappa)
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

**Finite bit-circuit construction and exact local cost/precision frontier; no new κ.**

For the restored six-register block `(H,T) -> (H,T+J3 H)`, one extra XOR lowers the best seven-gate positive peak from **5 to the support floor 4**, in both directions. The complete Pareto frontier `(XORs,F,B)` is **(7,5,5), (8,4,4)**. All preparation/restoration is paid; there are no extra registers, frame changes, COPY/ERASE events or recursive children inside the common-zero-frame block.

The census retains all **216** shortest circuits: 108 have `(F,B)=(5,5)`, 72 have `(6,6)`, and 36 have `(8,8)`. A separate algebraic support argument bounds both peaks below by four at every circuit length. The explicit eight-gate witness attains that bound. Its forward and reverse nonnegative transfer matrices are also componentwise no larger than the stated seven-gate witness, covering unequal incoming envelopes.

This increases the local ADD bill by one. It does not establish a new recursive profile, full-word guard improvement, supplier admission or multiplication exponent. No selected source or `upstream/` file changes.

## Task and overlap

- Base: `ef5f39403610d231a0c27e8a6b4f08c10209bcd6`.
- Contribution: `69e353410ae1e6f0555b5add9720f3e691a762b9`.
- OS seed **11**, bit supplier. [Task card and three candidates](https://github.com/bbMisk/integer-mult-bounds/blob/69e353410ae1e6f0555b5add9720f3e691a762b9/research/bit-j3-precision-seed11/TASK.json); [claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1507).
- Scope **changed** from `bit-helper-contract`: #1194/#1311 already cover the immediate H2/K substitution. This isolates precision cost at a complete local boundary.
- #1306, head `0d4c0069f1f4592833304a9ea6e61e676c566113`, already proves the seven-XOR minimum for J3. The new evidence concerns every shortest word's positive lift and the exact gate/precision tradeoff; the minimum itself is corroboration.
- #1341, head `becd4a2b6fad711914fe80f4344aef0008b30a28`, studies a fixed quad17 integer transfer. This package permits varying integer lifts of a different binary endpoint.
- Final overlap snapshot: 759 open PRs, 193 Discussion records, complete pagination, no warnings. Coverage limits and distinctions are in `OVERLAP.json`; no worldwide novelty claim.

The selected context remains #1094, κ = 0.001672660197076918, with #589 on #555. The complex primitive binds. Exact selected/assembly/review/source pins are retained as provenance.

## Validation

```sh
python3.12 -I -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/bit-j3-precision-seed11
```

Passed on **CPython 3.12.2**, including metadata/source pins and:

- Packed-row complete census using a `4 | <=3` split; all 810,000 four-gate prefixes and 27,931 backward words retained.
- Separate 64-input truth-table census using the opposite split, with dense integer positive matrices. Complete sorted-word digests, counts and positive classes agree. The implementations share no code, but use the same coverage principle.
- Eight semantic/input controls and **nine corrupted certificates rejected by both implementations** (18 rejection checks).
- Optimized isolated Python 3.14.6 replay and read-only minimal relocation; all 11 relocated files remained unchanged.
- Source-bound research baseline, clean Git diff and unchanged selected frontier/upstream inputs.

Expected final line: `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/bit-j3-precision-seed11 outcome=completed`.

The result is a finite exact certificate plus a written support/domination proof. No Lean, native multistage, full supplier, physical/common-frame, hosting, precision/tape or outer analytic replay was run. Hosted CI is separate from these local checks.

## Open next questions

The [README](https://github.com/bbMisk/integer-mult-bounds/blob/69e353410ae1e6f0555b5add9720f3e691a762b9/research/bit-j3-precision-seed11/README.md#open-next-questions) identifies the next useful check: find one exact J3 occurrence in a pinned R439 word, propagate its actual incoming bounds through both matrices, then price the extra XOR and replay the complete guards. The blocker is that no physical hosted occurrence or full invoice has been established here.
